pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Intermittent Porphyria (AIP) THE SMOKING GUN: Severe neurovisceral symptoms (hyponatremia, autonomic instability, neuropathy) triggered by fasting/sulfonamides, with urine oxidizing to a dark port-wine color upon ambient light exposure. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Acute Intermittent Porphyria is an autosomal dominant metabolic disorder caused by a deficiency in porphobilinogen deaminase (PBGD / HMBS), the third enzyme in the heme biosynthesis pathway. Exposure to precipitants (fasting, CYP450-inducing drugs like sulfonamides, infection, hormonal fluctuations) dramatically induces hepatic ALA synthase 1 (ALAS1). This results in the massive accumulation of neurotoxic porphyrin precursors: delta-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and porphobilinogen (PBG). ALA causes severe neurotoxicity, leading to autonomic dysfunction (tachycardia, hypertension), severe non-inflammatory abdominal pain, central neuropsychiatric disturbances, SIADH (inducing profound hyponatremia), and motor axonopathy (ascending motor paralysis). PBG polymerizes and oxidizes into porphobilin and porphyrins when exposed to air and light, producing the classic port-wine coloration of the urine.
